Charles Darwin, The Origin of Species.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/charles-darwin/the-origin-of-species

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Charles Darwin, the annotator, the author, the illustrator, the writer of an introduction, died 1882 (Wikidata Q1035, P570 = 1882-04-19).

First publication of the text used: 1859 (SE colophon: 'The Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection was published in 1859 by Charles Darwin.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: Standard Ebooks states that the text is in the United States public domain (rights statement below).
- Country of origin (United Kingdom): the text was first published there in 1859 by John Murray, London (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On_the_Origin_of_Species, country: United Kingdom, published 24 November 1859). Copyright there lasts for life plus 70 years after the death of the last surviving person named above. The last to die was Charles Darwin, in 1882, so the work entered the public domain there on 1 January 1953.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
